projection.basis: Each dimension scores below its reference band contributes (gap x coefficient) percentage points, with the low end at 45% of the coefficient. Coefficients differ by site type because the same defect costs a store and a portfolio different amounts.
assumptions: This is a model built from the gaps below the reference band, not a measurement of this site and not a forecast.
Dimensions that could not be read are left out of the range rather than guessed.
It assumes the recommended fixes actually ship and are maintained, and that traffic sources and seasonality stay as they are.
It counts the same visitor twice if two dimensions both gate them; treat the range as an order of magnitude, not a number to quote.
No analytics, ranking, ad spend or competitor data is read by this check, so it cannot know your real baseline.

stack.note: Read from the delivered HTML, script URLs and CSS text. Nothing was executed and nothing was fetched beyond the page and its same-origin stylesheets, so a marker that is absent here means "not found in this page", not "the site does not use it".

markup.note: Line numbers are counted from the start of the delivered HTML, one-based.

aiShape.basis: A word-list count plus sentence-length spread over the readable text of this one page. It is a shape detector, not an AI detector: no model is called, and a careful human writing in a generic register scores the same as a machine.
limits: It reads the delivered HTML only, so copy injected by script, held in an image, or behind a tab is invisible.
Chinese and English are both counted, but the lists are short: an unfamiliar register can pass.
It says nothing about whether the writing is any good, only how much of it is stock phrasing.

signals: headline is 3 words
a first action appears at 25% of the document (#main)
201 words of copy before any interaction
first byte in 62 ms
9 headings give the eye places to stop
hold.basis: A model over the first screen the HTML describes: headline length, how early the first real action appears, how much copy precedes it, first byte and document size. Scored against a band for the site type below.
limits: Real hold rate depends on the visitor's intent and the traffic source, which this check cannot see.
Nothing is rendered, so anything that only appears after script runs is not counted.
The figure is an order of magnitude to argue about, not a measurement of your traffic.

signals: 6 headings are phrased as questions
4 definition-shaped sentence(s) such as "X is a ..."
4 figure(s) with a unit
structured data: WebApplication, BreadcrumbList, ListItem, FAQPage
1326 words of copy, enough to answer a question
one H1 names the subject
geo.basis: A read of the delivered text for the four things an answer engine can lift verbatim: a question-shaped heading, a definition-shaped sentence, a figure with a unit, and structured data. It says nothing about ranking or about whether any engine will choose to cite the page.
limits: Search and answer engines are not queried. This is a property of the page, not a measurement of its visibility.
Copy rendered by script, inside an image, or behind a tab is invisible to this read.
A page can be highly quotable and still never be cited; the converse is also true.

signals: 3 contact routes
no case study, testimonial, price, process or timeframe on the page
trust markers: privacy notice, phone number in text, structured data: WebApplication, BreadcrumbList, ListItem
intent.basis: A model over what the delivered page offers a visitor who has already decided to act: how many contact routes exist, whether there is proof, whether trust markers are present, and how much friction the markup itself shows.
limits: It cannot see form completion, drop-off, or whether a route actually works. Nothing is submitted.
A site can convert with none of these markers, and fail with all of them; this only reads what the page states.
Any figure is a band for discussion, not a prediction of your enquiry rate.

signals: 3 field(s) to fill, none marked required
2 one-gesture route(s) as well: mailto or tel
friction.basis: A count of what the delivered markup asks of someone who has already decided to act: fields to fill, required marks, form groups, competing buttons, and whether a one-gesture route (mail, phone) exists at all. Nothing is submitted, and no form behaviour is observed.
limits: It cannot see whether a form works, validates, or is abandoned. Nothing is filled in or sent.
A form built or shown by script after load is invisible here.
Few fields is not the same as a good form: this reads cost, not clarity.

signals: no visible publication or update date in the copy
no Last-Modified header on the response
currency.basis: Three dated facts from one response: a copyright year in the text, any visible date, and a modified stamp either in structured data or on the HTTP response. It is a maintenance smell, not a judgement of the content.
limits: A page can be current with no date anywhere, and stale with a freshly bumped year.
Dates printed by script are invisible to a non-rendering read.
It says nothing about whether the offer is still true.

signals: 21 paragraph(s), average 36 words
longest unbroken block is 128 words
9 heading(s): about 147 words each
31 list item(s) break the copy up
25 bold run(s) mark the load-bearing phrases
scan.basis: Shape of the delivered copy, not its quality: average and longest paragraph length, the share of long paragraphs, words per heading, list items and bold runs. Built for someone who scans before they read.
limits: It counts delivered markup, so text set by script or baked into an image is invisible.
Short paragraphs can still be empty; long ones can still be good. This is shape, not judgement.
Mobile line length depends on rendering, which this check does not do.

limitations: Measured from one request by this server, not from a browser: no JavaScript was executed and no page was rendered.

The visual and interaction dimensions are read from HTML text and the same-origin stylesheets, not from what a visitor actually sees. Anything painted by script, an animation frame, or a cross-origin sheet is outside this read.
Core Web Vitals, layout stability, mobile rendering and anything behind a login are not measured.
The reference band for each dimension is an editorial target for the site type you chose, not a live crawl of competitor sites and not a ranking threshold.
The traffic range is a model over the gaps below those targets. It is not a forecast, not a promise, and not read from your analytics.
Back-end scoring reads response headers and cookie flags only; nothing behind the edge is visible.

The stack read lists markers found in the delivered HTML, script URLs and CSS text. Nothing was executed, so a marker that is absent means "not found in this page", not "the site does not use it"; bundled or server-side technologies are invisible here.

Residual SSRF note: hostnames are resolved and checked against private ranges before each connection, including every redirect hop and every stylesheet request, but DNS can change between the check and the request.
